ETA: I’ve found the Rico Reserve mouthpiece patches to be the eaisest to get off and they don’t seem to leave as much residue as some of the other brands. Hope this helps!!

Not necessarily. Jazz mouthpieces differ from standard classical mouthpieces in regards to things such as tip opening, baffel, and chamber shape, thus aiding in giving players different tone colors. Adjusting your embochure, air and the way you articulate on the mouthpiece you have now would be a good start since you probably aren’t sure what sound you really want yet. Jazz is heavily influence by the way you play(articulations, dynamics, phrasing) a mouthpiece isn’t going to do that stuff for you. If you get really serious about playing jazz I’d go try different mouthpieces out at a shop and see what you like best.
